title: Sum of paired preference signs
statement:
Label the six strict orderings of three alternatives $a,b,c$ by $k\in\{0,\dots,5\}$. For each ordering let $x_k\in\{-1,+1\}$ record the $a$-versus-$b$ comparison, taking the value $+1$ when $a$ is preferred to $b$ and $-1$ when $b$ is preferred to $a$, and let $y_k\in\{-1,+1\}$ record the $b$-versus-$c$ comparison in the same way, with $+1$ when $b$ is preferred to $c$ and $-1$ otherwise. Then
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{5} x_k\,y_k \;=\; -2.
\]
hypotheses_covered: none — a closed identity summed over the six orderings k ∈ {0,…,5}
replaced:
For each of the six strict orderings $k \in \{0,\dots,5\}$ of three alternatives
$a,b,c$, let $\mathrm{abPref}(k)$ and $\mathrm{bcPref}(k)$ be the Boolean preferences in
the $a$-vs-$b$ and $b$-vs-$c$ comparisons, and let $\sigma$ be the sign encoding. Then
the sum over all six orderings of the products of the encoded signs is
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{5} \sigma\big(\mathrm{abPref}(k)\big)\,\sigma\big(\mathrm{bcPref}(k)\big)
\;=\; -2.
\]
